implementation_notes: TypeScript compiles to JavaScript, so the realisation is ES module semantics with types on top: imports are evaluated before the importing module's body, a const initialiser runs at load, and a promise's executor runs at construction - 'acquire eagerly' means starting the work in a bootstrap module (or a framework hook such as onApplicationBootstrap) and exporting the settled value or a readiness promise, not exporting a factory that clients call later. Top-level await is the typed equivalent of a blocking start-up where ESM is available, and DI containers must be told to be eager: a provider that is never injected is never constructed, so warm-up code has to resolve it explicitly during bootstrap.
pitfalls: Module-scope side effects run in import order, so a bootstrap module imported after its consumers has already lost the race, and circular imports can bind an undefined pool.
Warm-up promises must handle their own rejection: a dangling rejected promise is an unhandled rejection, which Node treats as fatal by default.
DI containers resolve providers lazily, so a 'warm' service nobody injected is never constructed - resolve it explicitly at bootstrap or the acquisition never happens.
